messages.subject: Question regarding survey design
parts:
Hello,

I was wondering if you could please clarify something for me about a=
survey design from an existing data set. I tried to search in the archiv=
ed posts but am unsure what I am looking for.

There is an existing data set that was previously done in an attempt =
to estimate a free ranging dog population within a rural environment. Sam=
ple took place over three days. Each day a portion of the village was sur=
veyed in the morning and again in the same afternoon in the same area usi=
ng a line transect with a single observer. A perpendicular distance was c=
ollected for all observations. The overall covered are was approximately =
300 hectares. My question is: is it possible to combine the different day=
s of sampling in order to determine the overall dog density? Overall ther=
e are 201 observations. I first attempted to analysis the different days =
separately and was unsuccessful.=20

Any help would be greatly appreciated!

Thank you!
Jessie

messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: Question regarding survey design
parts:
Jessie:

You don't mention in your message what was unsuccessful about your first
analysis, so it is a bit hard to suggest a remedy. However ...

Seems you would be best advised to perhaps consider the days to be
strata, and you might wish to make inference about the average number of
dogs over the sampling events. The days might then be considered as a
sample of possible days on which you could conduct your surveys. Have a
look through Chapter 8 of the Distance Users Guide wherein a discussion
of strata as replicates can be found.
